results.note: Apologia Prophetae David included in NPNF2-10 (Ambrose: Selected Works and Letters, translated by H. de Romestin et al., 1896), a public-domain collection freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.

Apologia altera prophetae David likely included in NPNF2-10 though authorship disputed by some scholars (Erasmus, Tillemont questioned its authenticity). Appears in Archive.org listings with other Ambrose apologies and exegetical works in same collection.
De Abraham translated by Theodosia Tomkinson, published by Center for Traditionalist Orthodox Studies in 2000 (ISBN 9780911165425). Modern copyrighted translation.
De Cain et Abel in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Also included in FOTC 'Hexameron, Paradise, Cain and Abel' translated by John J. Savage (2004, copyrighted).
De Isaac et Anima (Isaac or the Soul) in FOTC Vol. 65 'Seven Exegetical Works' translated by Michael P. McHugh (CUA Press 1972), a modern copyrighted translation.
De Jacob et vita beata (Jacob and the Happy Life) in FOTC Vol. 65 'Seven Exegetical Works' translated by Michael P. McHugh (CUA Press 1972), a modern copyrighted translation.

De Tobia translated by Lois Miles Zucker, published as 'S. Ambrosii De Tobia: a commentary, with an introduction and translation' by Catholic University of America Press in 1933, a modern copyrighted scholarly edition.
De benedictionibus patriarcharum (The Patriarchs) in FOTC Vol. 65 'Seven Exegetical Works' translated by Michael P. McHugh (CUA Press 1972), a modern copyrighted translation.
De bono mortis (Death as a Good) in FOTC Vol. 65 'Seven Exegetical Works' translated by Michael P. McHugh (CUA Press 1972), a modern copyrighted translation.
De fuga saeculi included in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD), freely available online through CCEL and Tertullian.org.
De interpellatione Job et David (The Prayer of Job and David) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD) and also in FOTC Vol. 65 translated by McHugh (1972). NPNF version is freely accessible.
Enarrationes in XII psalmos Davidicos included in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD), freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.
Fragmentum is a very small fragment (146 words per manifest). Likely part of a larger work but cannot confirm if it is independently translated or only included as part of a parent work.
Hexaemeron included in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Also available in modern FOTC 'Hexameron, Paradise, Cain and Abel' translated by John J. Savage (2004). NPNF version is freely accessible.

Anacephalaeosis Historiae de excidio Hierosolymitanae urbis is a pseudo-Ambrosian work (Ambrosian attribution disputed; likely 9th-century Carolingian composition). This is a summary of Pseudo-Hegesippus' De excidio Iudaeorum. No English translation found in standard patristic collections.

Commentarius in Cantica canticorum (Commentary on Song of Songs): Work exists in Latin (PL 15:1945-2060) but no English translation identified in NPNF, FOTC, ACW, or other major patristic series despite searches.

De excidio urbis Hierosolymitanae (On the Destruction of Jerusalem): While sometimes listed under Ambrose, this is actually Pseudo-Hegesippus' work (4th-cent. adaptation of Josephus' Jewish War). English translation exists though attribution is complex; content appears in patristic collections.

Expositio Evangelii secundum Lucam (Exposition on Luke's Gospel) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Also translated by Theodosia Tomkinson (2000) as 'Exposition of the Holy Gospel According to Saint Luke with Fragments on the Prophecy of Isaias'. NPNF version freely accessible.
Expositio in psalmum David CXVIII (Exposition on Psalm 118) included in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available through CCEL and Tertullian.org.
De Spiritu Sancto (On the Holy Spirit) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD) translated by H. de Romestin, E. de Romestin and H.T.F. Duckworth. Freely accessible online on CCEL, New Advent, and Tertullian.org.
De excessu fratris sui Satyrus (On the Decease of His Brother Satyrus): Two addresses included in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.
De incarnationis Dominicae sacramento in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Also in FOTC Vol. 44 'Theological and Dogmatic Works' translated by Roy J. Deferrari (1963). NPNF version freely accessible.

De lapsu virginis consecratae (On the Fall of a Consecrated Virgin): Authorship uncertain; possibly by Nicetas of Remesiana rather than Ambrose himself. Work exists in Latin (PL XVI:367-384) but no English translation found in standard sources.
De mysteriis (On the Mysteries) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Also in FOTC Vol. 44 translated by Deferrari (1963) and Thompson/Strawley edition (1919). NPNF version freely accessible.
De obitu Theodosii oratio (Oration on the Death of Theodosius) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.
De obitu Valentiniani consolatio (Consolation on the Death of Valentinian) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.
De officiis ministrorum (On the Duties of the Clergy) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Also modern OUP edition with translation/commentary. NPNF version freely accessible.
De poenitentia (Two Books Concerning Repentance) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.

De sacramentis in Thompson/Strawley edition 'On the Mysteries and the Treatise on the Sacraments' (Macmillan 1919, now PD). Also in NPNF2-10 and FOTC Vol. 44 (Deferrari 1963). Thompson/Strawley version freely accessible online.
De viduis (Concerning Widows) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.
De virginitate in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org as 'Concerning Virginity'.

Epistolarum classis II (Letters, second collection) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD) which includes selections from Ambrose's 91 epistles. Also in FOTC Vol. 26 translated by Mary Melchior Beyenka (1954). NPNF version freely accessible.
Exhortatio virginitatis (Exhortation to Virginity) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.

Fragmentum ex Theodoreto desumptum (Fragment taken from Theodoret): Very small work (1,021 words per manifest). Likely a fragment extracted from a larger work; unclear if independently translated or only included as part of a parent work in collections.
Hymni (Four Ambrosian Hymns) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.

Sermones (Sermons): Small collection (3,925 words per manifest). Fragmentary sermons from Ambrose; not clearly identified as a distinct complete work in NPNF or FOTC tables of contents. May be fragments included elsewhere.
De Elia et jejunio (On Elias and Fasting) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.

De Joseph Patriarcha (On the Patriarch Joseph): Referenced in scholarly sources and archive.org catalogs with other Ambrose exegetical works, but not explicitly confirmed in NPNF2-10 table of contents fetched. Possibly in FOTC Vol. 65 or Vol. 140 but cannot confirm.

De Nabuthe Jezraelita (On Naboth) translated by Martin McGuire, published as 'S. Ambrosii De Nabuthae: a commentary, with an introduction and translation' by Catholic University of America Press in 1927, a modern copyrighted scholarly edition.
De Noe et Arca (Treatise on Noah) in FOTC Vol. 140 'Treatises on Noah and David' translated by Brian P. Dunkle, SJ (CUA Press 2022), a modern copyrighted translation. Also likely in NPNF2-10.
De fide (Five Books on the Faith/Exposition of the Christian Faith) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD) translated by H. de Romestin, E. de Romestin and H.T.F. Duckworth. Freely available on CCEL and New Advent.
De institutione virginis (On the Training of a Virgin) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.
De paradiso (On Paradise) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Also in FOTC 'Hexameron, Paradise, Cain and Abel' translated by John J. Savage (2004). NPNF version freely accessible.
De virginibus (Concerning Virgins) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD). Freely available on CCEL and Tertullian.org.

Epistolarum classis I (Letters, first collection) in NPNF2-10 (1896, PD) which includes selections from Ambrose's 91 epistles. Also in FOTC Vol. 26 translated by Mary Melchior Beyenka (1954). NPNF version freely accessible.
